messages:
marta: Quick RFC follow-up — I want to propose a long-term refactor to split eng-runtime into two clearer services: a data-plane "inference-executor" that handles low-latency token generation/KV cache/model kernels, and a control-plane "inference-control" that owns model lifecycle, routing, batching policy, and telemetry. Goal: reduce coupling, make rollout/testing safer, and pay down model-loading tech debt. Thoughts?

sujeet: +1 on separation. We've piled a lot of orthogonal concerns into runtime (model loading, batching, auth, metrics). Splitting will let us optimize execution paths without risking control-plane regressions.

olivia: Biggest tradeoff I see is cross-service latency and complexity for KV/cache ownership. If executor doesn't own KV cache we pay network hops on every request. Do we plan shared in-memory cache or a cache-per-executor? :thinking: 

ben: We should treat KV/cache as part of the data-plane. Keep it local to executor to avoid extra RTTs. Control-plane can push model metadata and cache invalidation events.

marta: Agreed — data-plane owns hot KV/cache and model artifact memory. Control-plane owns image distribution + pinned versions + health checks.

nina: We need clear RPC contracts. Proposed: gRPC for data-plane (binary, low-overhead) and REST/gRPC for control-plane APIs. Version all endpoints with semantic API versioning.

mike: Also flagging testing/CI debt: we rely on full end-to-end infra tests that are flaky. With split, we can unit-test control-plane and run a lightweight executor emulator for control-plane test matrix. That should speed up safety checks.

ashley: Migration plan idea: phase 0 = extract control-only endpoints from runtime and add a thin proxy; phase 1 = run control-plane as new service, keep runtime in compatibility mode; phase 2 = flip routing and start removing compatibility layers. Each phase gated by canary metrics and smoke tests.

marta: That aligns with what I had in mind. Can we draft explicit acceptance criteria per phase? Example metrics: p50/p99 latency on data-plane, model load success rate, cold-start times, traces correlated to request id.

sujeet: Acceptance criteria suggestion:
- Phase 0: control endpoints extracted, unit tests added, no change to data-plane latency (<= +2ms p50).
- Phase 1: control-plane serving >90% traffic for metadata/config operations; data-plane latency within SLO; model rollouts tested on canary pool.
- Phase 2: compatibility mode removed, full e2e tests passing in staging for 48h, deploy to prod.

ben: Operationally we need a contract for rollback. If control-plane introduces bad routing, data-plane should keep a local fallback config embedded in the container image. Fallback config updated via image releases.

olivia: That means images will embed last-known-good policies. We should add feature flags to force local-only mode (useful during control-plane outage).

marta: Good call. Also thinking about schema management for control-plane messages: use protobuf + schema registry for compatibility checks. Example proto for model manifest below: 
```proto
message ModelManifest {
  string model_id = 1;
  string version = 2;
  repeated string artifacts = 3;
  map<string,string> runtime_config = 4;
}
```

nina: Love the proto approach. We should also define semantic rules for forward/backward compatibility and include linting in CI.

mike: Resource ownership note: data-plane should expose a small set of health and resource metrics that control-plane can query, but control-plane must not be on the critical path for token generation. Keep path: request -> executor local model + KV -> generate tokens.

ashley: For deployment, propose we create a "refactor-stability" squad (2 engs runtime + 1 infra + 1 SRE) to own the phased rollout and monitoring dashboards. Timeline: 8 weeks for Phase 0, 8 weeks Phase 1, 6 weeks Phase 2 + buffer.

sujeet: Add a tech-debt ledger entry for each area we're touching (model-loading race conditions, config coupling, flaky e2e tests). Prioritize fixes with measurable SLO improvements.

marta: Action items:
- @sujeet: sketch RPC surface and proto catalog (due EOW)
- @ben: design cache invalidation & fallback plan + perf budget (due +2w)
- @nina: CI linting rules for proto/schema and compatibility tests (due +2w)
- @ashley: propose squad and schedule for phased rollout (due +3d)
- @mike: audit current e2e tests and propose lightweight executor emulator (due +1w)

deploy-bot: Note: created ticket INF-1342 for "split runtime control/data plane RFC follow-up" assigned to marta.

marta: Thanks all. If no objections by EOD tomorrow I'll convert this into a short RFC appendix and attach the initial phase acceptance criteria. :+1: 

ashley: No objections from me, will start squad charter.

ben: 👍

nina: 👍

olivia: One more thing — we should schedule a cross-team sync with product to ensure rollout policies don't change customer expectations unexpectedly.

marta: Agreed, I'll loop in product in the RFC.
